newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 60 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed. [CORRECTED 20:41 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 60 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed. [CORRECTED 20:41 GMT]

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 40 billion bolivar ($127 million) auction of 180-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 17.65 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer 10 billion bolivars ($42 million) in 269-day bills with a 18.03 percent coupon, and another 10 billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 18.42 percent coupon.
(Corrects amount of bills to be sold to 10 billion each from 20 billion each.)
Eighteen billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are down from last week's 60 billion bolivar issue. Then 180-, 270- and 359-day notes carried 18.45, 18.87, and 19.3 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that softened between 50 and 100 basis points along the curve to 17.65, 20.78 and 21.32 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
